finding.summary: The accepted self-hosted runner can fail before product regressions execute because the persistent GitHub Actions workspace contains root-owned Python bytecode under runtime/claycode_eval_v1/__pycache__. Checkout cleanup therefore cannot reliably reset the tree as the frankrunner user. A run-unique RUNNER_TEMP checkout avoids that contaminated persistent worktree for the self.root current-head boundary workflow, but the repair is not promoted until the corrected workflow passes its existing semantic/static gates.
finding.scientific_boundary: Checkout/runner failures are infrastructure evidence, not evidence for or against Frank/ClayCode semantics. Per-workflow isolation does not repair the root ownership source globally.

accepted_target_forensics.interpretation: Multiple-listener and multiple-worker hypotheses were not observed in this run; ownership contamination was directly observed.

prior_checkout_failure.evidence: self-hosted current-head checkout cleanup failed with EACCES on analyzer.cpython-312.pyc before tests ran

hypothesis.statement: For regression workflows that only need a clean exact-SHA tree, fetching the tested SHA into a run/attempt-unique RUNNER_TEMP tree as the runner user will decouple product validation from foreign-owned residue in the persistent Actions workspace.

strongest_counterhypothesis.statement: Per-run isolation only masks the current persistent-workspace symptom. A test or privileged subprocess could still create foreign-owned files in RUNNER_TEMP, and the global source of root-owned bytecode remains unresolved; the correct long-term repair must identify and remove the privilege/ownership source and restore ordinary checkout cleanliness.
